FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards after the draft finalized by the Artificial 
Limbs, Rehabilitation Appliances and Equipment for Persons with Disabilitv, Sectional Committee and approval 
bv the Medical Equipment and Hospital Planning Division Council. 


Surgical ankle boot with broad toe (child and adult sizes) are to be used bv orthopedicallv challenged invalids to 
accommodate, correct the deformities of ankle foot disorders. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex A. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analvsis shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 1960 Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised). The number of significant places retained in the 
rounded off value shall be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 17194 : 2019 


Indian Standard 


SURGICAL ANKLE BOOT WITH BROAD TOE 
( CHILD AND ADULT SIZE ) — 
SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies the dimensions, design 
parameters and material requirements for construction 
of surgical ankle boot with broad toe (child and adult 
sizes) in standard sizes (English point svstem). 


1.2 This standard covers boot sizes 1 to 13 for children 
and boot sizes 1 to 13 for adults. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed below contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
listed below: 


IS No. Title 

579 : 2017 Vegetable tanned sole leather — 
Specification ( fourth revision) 

1720 : 1978 Cotton sewing threads (second 
revision) 

2961 : 1973 Specification for chrome retan 
finished upper leather ( first revision) 

4512 : 1978 Specification for footwear lasts, 
wooden ( first revision) 

5041 : 1978 Specification for footvvear and 
stationary eyelets ( first revision) 

3TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, terminology and 
definition of various parts given in 3.1 to 3.7 as shown 
in Fig. 1A shall apply. 


3.1 Boot Length — The longitudinal length betvveen 
mid-section of heel and middle finger of the boot as 
defined in Fig. 1B vvith top surface of the boot kept 
parallel to the ground. 


3.2 Boot Height — The maximum height of the boot 
at heel section. 


3.3 Heel Height — The distance measured betvveen 
ground and top surface of the heel attached to the 


boot, vvhile top surface of the boot kept parallel to the 
ground. 


3.4 Heel VVidth — The maximum vvidth of the heel as 
defined in Fig. 1B. 


3.5 Toe Break — Proximal area in the forefoot region 
which bend/flexes while walking. 


3.6 Toe Circumference — The circumference 
measured at toe break (tread line) section. 


3.7 Toe Width — The maximum width of toe break 
(tread line) section. 


4 MATERIALS 


4.1 Boot Upper 


Boot upper shall be made from good quality leather 
chrome upper (soft) retanned, five hair cell finish, black 
colour and thickness 1.5 mm + 0.1 mm as per IS 2961. 


4.2 Insole 


Insole shall be from vegetable tanned, natural colour 
leather of 3 mm nominal thickness as per IS 579. 


4.3 Lining 


Lining shall be made from softy leather chrome, tanned, 
natural colour of thickness 0.9 to 1.2 mm. 


4.4 Sole 


Sole shall be made from vegetable tanned leather, 
natural colour of 5 mm nominal thickness as per IS 579. 


4.5 Heel 


Heel shall be formed using 4 to 6 layers of sole leather. 
The shape of the heel shall be made as per the plaster 
cast mould of the deformed foot. 


5 CONSTRUCTIONS 


5.1 Welt 


The boots shall be of welt type construction with welt 
attached to the insole and the upper around the outer 
edge of the boots. Welt shall be stitched with cotton/ 
linen thread of matching color and conforming to 
variety No. 34 of IS 1720. The number of stitches shall 
be 2.5 stitches per 25 mm minimum. The nominal 
thickness of welt shall be 2 mm for children sizes 
and 2.5 mm for adult sizes. 


IS 17194 : 2019 


5.2 Upper 


The upper and lining shall be pasted and stitched vvith 
cotton sevving thread of matching color of upper and 
conforming to varietv No. 32 of IS 1720. The number 
of stitches shall be minimum 12 stitches per 25 mm. 


5.3 Sole 


The outer sole shall be attached to the vvelt by stitching 
vvith cotton / nylon sevving thread of matching colour 
and fixed with steel shank at mid shoe/boot area and 
confirming to variety No. 34 of IS 1720. The number of 
stitches shall be minimum of 6 per 25 mm. 


5.4 Heel 


The heel shall be provided loose (not attached with the 
boots) with each pair. Heel thickness for boots shall be 
as given in Table 1.

6 SIZES AND DIMENSIONS 


The dimensional details vvith permissible tolerances 
for boot ankle child and adult sizes (1 to 13) as 
indicated in Table 2 are incorporated vvith dimensional 
variable -- 10 percent matching vvith the deformed foot 
circumference. 


7 SHAPE 


The performance of the boots depends upon its correct 
fitment with the foot at various places. The shape of the 
boot has to be made, so that it provides tight/loose/snug 
fitting with the foot as indicated in Fig. 1B, Fig. 1C, 
Fig. ID, Fig. IE and Fig. IF. 

NOTE — Sets of shoe lasts suitable for hand shoemaking 


process as per IS 4512 shall be used for each size in child and 
adult sizes boots. 


8 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 


8.1 Upper 


8.1.1 The upper shall be attached to the lining in such 
a manner that it is free from wrinkles and non-sticking 
areas. 


8.1.2 A leather stiffener shall be provided and in case 
of soft heel inner counter to be provided for painful 
posterior heel. 


8.1.3 A jug loop at the top edge of the upper on the back 
side shall be provided in all cases.

8.3 Sole 


The sole shall be securelv attached to the welt bv 
stitching. The sole shall be reasonably flat along its 
length and shall not have marked curve in cross-section. 
The filling between insole and outer sole is adjusted to 
maintain flatness of the sole. 


8.4 Socks 
Full length socks shall be provided for all boots. 


8.5 General 


The general workmanship and finish shall be of good 
qualitv as per the trade practice. The boots shall be 
supplied dulv polished with laces provided. The quarter 
shall be stitched securelv where it attaches with the toe 
to ensure long life without damage to stitches. 


9 MARKING 


9.1 All boots shall be indelibly and clearly marked with 
its sizes and make or manufactures trade-mark on the 
inside of the quarter near the top. 


9.1.1 The size shall also be marked centrally on the 
bottom surface of the sole in the mid foot area. 


9.1.2 The packages shall also be marked with sizes of 
the boots and make or manufactures trade-mark. 


9.2 BIS Certificate Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of 
this standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the Bureau 
of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the Rules and 
Regulations framed thereunder, and the product(s) may 
be marked with the Standard Mark. 


10 PACKAGING 


The packaging of boots shall be as agreed to between 
the purchaser and the manufacturer/supplier. 


IS 17194 : 2019

Bureau of Indian Standards 


BIS is a statutorv institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 to promote harmonious 
development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods and attending to 
connected matters in the country. 


Copyright 


BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form vvithout 
the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of implementing the 
standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. Enquiries relating to 
copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 


Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 
‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards: Monthly Additions’.
